summary:
Farm ClimeTech is a global app that gives every farmer, anywhere on Earth, climate answers built from the data of their own field.

NASA satellites observe the whole planet every day, but that data rarely reaches the people who work the land. Farm ClimeTech closes that gap: a farmer in Uruguay, Kenya, India or EEUU pins their field on a satellite map, and the app answers two questions with local data for that exact point: where the climate risk is, and which crop rotation holds up best.

For any coordinate it combines NASA satellite layers (soil moisture, rainfall, vegetation, land temperature), a 12-month risk calendar from 40 years of NASA POWER daily climate records, and local soil properties, then ranks four crop rotations by climate resilience and sends plain-language alerts that say what to check and when.

It works on a phone, keeps the last data offline, and uses AI to explain results in simple words. One global platform, local answers: we start in Uruguay and the same model works on any farm with a phone.
details:
Farm ClimeTech is a mobile-first web app. The farmer searches a place or taps the satellite map to pin a field. The app then shows: (1) today's field condition from NASA satellite layers (true color, NDVI vegetation, land surface temperature, soil moisture, precipitation); (2) a 12-month climate-risk calendar for drought, heat and excess rain, computed from 40 years of NASA POWER daily data; (3) four crop rotations ranked by climate resilience with the reasons behind each score; (4) soil properties from ISRIC SoilGrids; (5) alerts written as actions; and (6) a printable farm report.

React + TypeScript + Vite frontend with Leaflet maps and NASA GIBS tiles; a Node.js server that keeps all API keys server-side and calls Google Gemini to explain results in plain language (falls back to a demo mode without a key). Security: CSP and security headers, rate limiting, input validation, no secrets in the browser. Deployed on Render.

Free satellite data becomes a decision a farmer can act on: what to plant, when to irrigate, when to protect the crop. Built for Uruguay first, replicable anywhere.

Inspired by Apollo 8's Earthrise: the same eyes that showed us our fragile planet now watch over each field. Our 30-second film uses real Apollo 8 onboard audio.
